what_this_is: Check the files and folders a person's own list says can be got back; move eligible paths to recoverable Trash only on a real run. Physical bytes freed are unmeasured.

payload.label: Move eligible files from my list to Trash
payload.job: Move files and folders my list says I can get back to recoverable Trash after checking the listed sources and recipes
payload.description: Give 1 to 100 rows, each { id, value }, and the folder granted for change. Eligibility requires the saved state, no hold, a regular file or folder inside the grant, no top-level link or git-tracked files, at least one source address or recipe, every source answering, every recipe tracked, unchanged and pushed, and no changes within the quiet hours or during the check. A source answering proves availability only, not identical or complete recovery bytes. dry_run defaults to true and moves nothing. A real run asks the native macOS Trash service; it never permanently deletes or empties Trash, and a denied move returns no next_value. Only a confirmed move returns next_value with the moved-to-Trash state. path_bytes and trashed_path_bytes describe observed path allocation, not reclaimed storage; freed_bytes is null because it is unmeasured. The change-a-folder grant may refuse Trash access; this tool never widens it. Field names and state words are DATA in read-data/kept-file-shape.json, overridden by shape.

rows.description: Rows of the person's list of files and how to get them back

dry_run.description: true (the default) moves nothing; false requests recoverable native Trash moves within the current grant

shape.description: Only the field names, state words or quiet_hours that differ from read-data/kept-file-shape.json

path_bytes.description: Observed path allocation for eligible paths; null when the path check did not establish it

freed_bytes.description: Unmeasured: moving to Trash does not establish physical disk space reclaimed
